items.title: v2.1.199
items.bullet_md: - 🛠 **[v2.1.199](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.199)** — _Claude Code releases_. — Stacked slash-skills (`/skill-a /skill-b`) now load all leading skills up to 5, SSL handshake failures skip retries and surface the fix hint immediately, and partial streaming output survives mid-stream API errors instead of being discarded.

score_components.taste_reason: Concrete release with stacked slash-skill invocation, SSL fix hints, and streaming error handling — directly useful for daily Claude Code users.

items.title: JetBrains 7.0.1-rc.14
items.bullet_md: - 🛠 **[JetBrains 7.0.1-rc.14](https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/releases/tag/jetbrains%2Fv7.0.1-rc.14)** — _Kilo Code releases_. — Adds Agent Behavior settings and a richer model picker with routed model info and clearer badges, plus more reliable backend startup recovery when event streams stall or reconnect.

score_components.taste_reason: Niche JetBrains plugin RC with Agent Behavior settings and backend recovery; narrow appeal to an IDE-specific audience.

items.title: v1.41.0
items.bullet_md: - 🛠 **[v1.41.0](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/releases/tag/v1.41.0)** — _Goose releases_. — Adds iFlytek Spark and Astron MaaS providers, an `--edit` flag for pre-fork conversation editing, GLM-5.2 model support, global hints from `~/.agents/AGENTS.md`, and desktop localization for 8 new languages.

score_components.taste_reason: Adds iFlytek/ Astron/ Fireworks providers plus desktop l10n — useful OSS agent tooling update but incremental.

items.title: v1.40.0
items.bullet_md: - 🛠 **[v1.40.0](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/releases/tag/v1.40.0)** — _Goose releases_. — Adds `/status`, `/model`, and `/goal` slash commands for session insights, model switching, and self-evaluation, plus `goose review` for local code review and a hooks system for custom extensibility.

score_components.taste_reason: New /status, /model, /goal slash commands and local review — solid incremental Goose release with no headline number.

items.title: Microsoft launches $2.5 billion "Frontier Company" to embed 6,000 AI engineers inside enterprise clients
items.bullet_md: - 📰 **[Microsoft launches $2.5 billion "Frontier Company" to embed 6,000 AI engineers inside enterprise clients](https://the-decoder.com/microsoft-launches-2-5-billion-frontier-company-to-embed-6000-ai-engineers-inside-enterprise-clients/)** — _The Decoder_. — Microsoft is putting $2.5 billion behind Frontier Company, embedding 6,000 engineers directly with enterprise clients — positioning itself as a platform-neutral alternative to the dedicated deployment arms OpenAI and Anthropic have each set up.

score_components.taste_reason: Concrete $2.5B/6,000-engineer number on Microsoft embedding AI staff inside enterprises — major industry signal, not in state-of-ai.

items.title: Anthropic says it cut 80 percent of Claude Code's system prompt because Fable 5 models "want a smaller system prompt"
items.bullet_md: - 📰 **[Anthropic says it cut 80 percent of Claude Code's system prompt because Fable 5 models "want a smaller system prompt"](https://the-decoder.com/anthropic-says-it-cut-80-percent-of-claude-codes-system-prompt-because-fable-5-models-want-a-smaller-system-prompt/)** — _The Decoder_. — Where earlier model generations needed more rules and examples to stay on track, Anthropic found its Fable 5 class actually performs worse with too much steering — it cut 80 percent of Claude Code's system prompt after realising the model is more imaginative than the examples it was given.

score_components.taste_reason: Specific 80% reduction number plus the Fable-5-wants-smaller-prompts rationale — directly relevant and surprising for daily Claude Code users.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg tells staff that AI agents haven’t progressed as quickly as he’d hoped
items.bullet_md: - 📰 **[Mark Zuckerberg tells staff that AI agents haven't progressed as quickly as he'd hoped](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/02/mark-zuckerberg-tells-staff-that-ai-agents-havent-progressed-as-quickly-as-hed-hoped/)** — _TechCrunch AI_. — Despite reassigning 7,000 employees to AI groups and planning $145 billion in infrastructure spend this year, Zuckerberg told staff at an internal town hall that AI agents haven't accelerated as Meta expected — admitting the payoff from its restructuring hasn't come to fruition yet.

score_components.taste_reason: Notable admission from a major player that resonates with anyone building agents, but no specifics — no metrics, no timeline, just a vague 'not as quick as hoped' quote.

items.title: Meta quietly launches vibe-coded gaming app Pocket
items.bullet_md: - 📰 **[Meta quietly launches vibe-coded gaming app Pocket](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/02/meta-quietly-launches-vibe-coded-gaming-app-pocket/)** — _TechCrunch AI_. — Meta repurposed the team behind vibe-coded gaming platform Gizmo into its own Pocket app, letting anyone type a prompt and get a shareable mini game — joining a growing lineup of AI creation tools alongside Vibes for AI video and Meta AI for images.

score_components.taste_reason: Actual product launch from a major lab with a concrete capability (text-to-mini-game), but experimental/early — worth a click for the curious but not urgent.

items.title: New York City educators and industry leaders gathered at Google’s offices to shape the future of AI in classrooms.
items.bullet_md: - 🔵 **[New York City educators and industry leaders gathered at Google's offices to shape the future of AI in classrooms.](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/education/nyc-ai-summit/)** — _Google AI blog_. — Google, the New York Jobs CEO Council, and Urban Assembly convened 150 education and industry leaders for an AI-in-classrooms summit, the throughline being that as AI streamlines workflows, human skills like adaptability and critical judgment matter more, with hands-on sessions on Google AI mode, NotebookLM, and aiEDU's Vibe Coding.

score_components.taste_reason: Google AI education summit — PR event with 150 attendees, no substance for an AI engineering audience.

items.title: Fable 5 vs GPT 5.6 Sol: The Early Results
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Fable 5 vs GPT 5.6 Sol: The Early Results](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y24lF1q4SFY) — **AI Explained** (18m03s). — AI Explained compares Fable 5 against GPT 5.6 Sol early results, covering model benchmarks, Sonnet 5, and a US government equity seizure in OpenAI.

score_components.taste_reason: Introduces new model names (Fable 5, GPT 5.6 Sol, Sonnet 5) not in state-of-ai from a credible analysis channel; concrete comparison content that extends the frontier models row with genuinely new information.

items.title: Build an MCP Server
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Build an MCP Server](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=izbkb5XPhBg) — **4Geeks Academy** (1h06m). — 4Geeks Academy hosts a live session on building an MCP server to give AI agents access to custom tools.

score_components.taste_reason: Basic tutorial on MCP server building; MCP is already established in the known baseline and a 1h06m live session from a general academy offers no novel architecture or benchmark data.

items.title: GLM 5.2 + GPT-5.5 (My Workflow): This is the BEST WAY TO CODE RIGHT NOW!
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [GLM 5.2 + GPT-5.5 (My Workflow): This is the BEST WAY TO CODE RIGHT NOW!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gNFpbVWq5jw) — **AICodeKing** (13m42s). — AICodeKing demonstrates a coding workflow combining OpenDesign, OpenCode, Requesty, and Railway to switch between models like GLM-5.2 and GPT-5.5 for staged code generation and interface design.

score_components.taste_reason: Clickbait title caps it; workflow recaps known models (GLM-5.2, GPT-5.5 already in state-of-ai) from a low-credibility YouTube channel with no novel techniques or benchmarks.

items.title: Laguna XS 2.1: Poolside's Local Coding Agent Tested - Nine Languages
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Laguna XS 2.1: Poolside's Local Coding Agent Tested - Nine Languages](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fobY4W_0_2g) — **Fahd Mirza** (10m50s). — Fahd Mirza tests Laguna XS 2.1, a 33B model with 3B activated parameters per token from Poolside, designed for agentic coding across nine languages.

score_components.taste_reason: Concrete model architecture detail (33B/3B activated) from Poolside not yet in state-of-ai's open-weights row, but a YouTube review from a smaller channel — useful for local-model enthusiasts, not a must-read.

items.title: Easy Way to Use LM Studio with Unreal Engine 5.8 | MCP Server Integration & Run Local AI Models
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Easy Way to Use LM Studio with Unreal Engine 5.8 | MCP Server Integration & Run Local AI Models](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BtXPDsNqxQU) — **Unreal Fusion** (7m24s). — Unreal Fusion shows how to connect LM Studio with Unreal Engine 5.8 using the Model Context Protocol to run local AI models in game development.

score_components.taste_reason: Extremely niche game-dev integration tutorial with no novel facts; a narrow audience of Unreal Engine developers using local AI — irrelevant for the general senior-AI reader.

items.title: Fable 5 Won Every Test I Ran… Then I Saw The Bill
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Fable 5 Won Every Test I Ran… Then I Saw The Bill](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MH7aDyULylU) — **Income stream surfers** (13m24s). — Income stream surfers runs Fable 5 through real coding tests inside Harbor Build and discovers strong results come with a steep token cost.

score_components.taste_reason: Fable 5 real-world coding test with cost analysis — concrete bill shock detail useful for anyone evaluating Fable 5.

items.title: Fable 5 is WILD...
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Fable 5 is WILD...](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GPxUhrdDbKE) — **Wes Roth** (24m28s). — Wes Roth demonstrates setting up Fable 5 through the Higgsfield platform as an MCP, CLI, or skill in 30 seconds across Claude, Cursor, and Hermes Agent.

score_components.taste_reason: Wes Roth demonstrating Fable 5 setup across Claude/Cursor/Hermes Agent — practical demo but thin on new data beyond the Higgsfield platform release.

items.title: This FREE Tool Turns ANY PDF into Perfect Markdown (MinerU Live Test)
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [This FREE Tool Turns ANY PDF into Perfect Markdown (MinerU Live Test)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Xkt6ydLIg4) — **Prompt Engineer** (3m21s). — Useful for RAG pipeline builders — MinerU parses PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX into structured Markdown or JSON, now at 73.1k GitHub stars with v3.4 boosting OCR accuracy ~11% via PP-OCRv6.

score_components.taste_reason: Clickbait title ('ANY PDF into Perfect') for a basic PDF-to-Markdown tool demo; no benchmarks, no novel architecture, and there are dozens of equivalent extraction tools — pure skim-past.

items.title: AI was HARD until I Learned these 10 Concepts
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [AI was HARD until I Learned these 10 Concepts](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-qC_1A_WZbs) — **Andrew Codesmith** (15m45s). — Covers 10 foundational AI engineering concepts with hands-on examples for developers new to the field.

score_components.taste_reason: Beginner listicle with clickbait title; zero concrete benchmarks or novel techniques for a senior AI engineer.

items.title: Autoresearch: The feedback loop behind self-improving agents
items.bullet_md: - 📝 **[Autoresearch: The feedback loop behind self-improving agents](https://www.latent.space/p/autoresearch-introspection)** — _Latent Space (swyx)_. — Latent Space interviews Introspection CEO Roland Gavrilescu (ex-xAI) on autoresearch — outer feedback loops where agents maintain the system itself, organized as portable agent recipes in a Git-based workflow.

score_components.taste_reason: Latent Space interview on autoresearch and self-improving agent loops — credible source, concrete framework discussion, relevant to agent engineers.

items.title: SLIM-RL: Risk-Budgeted Random-Masking RL for Diffusion LLMs Without Trajectory Slicing
items.bullet_md: - 🧪 **[SLIM-RL: Risk-Budgeted Random-Masking RL for Diffusion LLMs Without Trajectory Slicing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00208)** — _arXiv cs.CL_. — A new RL method for diffusion LLMs that matches TraceRL math accuracy at under half the training data, beating it by 6.32% on MATH500 and 11.05% on GSM8K without trajectory slicing.

score_components.taste_reason: Technical RL method for diffusion LLMs that claims to cut trajectory-slicing cost, but no benchmark comparisons to TraceRL or other baselines are given; interesting to diffusion-ML researchers only.
